output.quote: Ok I do want release management in R1. Here's how I see it working, we base it on git flow.
output.summary: Approved G1025 design attempt 3 (git-flow release branching), after three review rounds (8 then 4 findings, all fixed). It honours the owner's interview answers O1-O4: goal branches keep rebasing and only release->dev back-merges are merges; cutting release/N opens dev to N+1; finishing merges into main and back into dev, keeps the release branch, and hotfix lines exist; the cut is offered when every release N goal is closed done. One open release line at a time; line goals on a shipped `release` graph; a closed-goal ledger from commit trailers; frontier-computed waits; record-only hotfix sync; single-use hotfix names. Recorded at approval: the capability is named `release_lines` (G1027's naming), not `branching`; the policy block stays settings.branching. Implementation must also delete G1025's G1017 pending row.

responses.review_design:2:1: fixed: §6/§8/D20. Both waits are now frontier states, recomputed on every evaluation and never recorded as blocks. base waits release_sync while upstream[g].merged_in_target shows a merged dependency's commit missing from the target tip. finish waits line_members_open from the ledger: line_complete is now on both approve_finish and finish. If the op hits either state in a race, it returns a time wait with retry_after. Tests: the sync lands, then base runs with no other change; a late member is cancelled, then finish runs on the existing approval.
responses.review_design:2:2: fixed: §7/§5.4/D21. On hotfix lines, sync is no longer skipped. It runs in record-only mode (ready when the hotfix tip differs from its recorded merged; it records merged = hotfix tip and merges nothing). So approve_finish's sync input is the hotfix tip, and finish's tip check is the same for both line kinds. Test: a member merged after the approval makes approve_finish stale.
responses.review_design:2:3: fixed: §7/D22. Hotfix names are single-use. new/edit refuse a flow.hotfix that names a closed hotfix line (from its Line trailer), with the hint 'choose a new name'. hotfix start refuses when the key scan finds only a closed line, and returns recovered only for an open one. Test added.
responses.review_design:2:4: fixed: §3.1/§3.2/D6. The trailer is now Closed: <reason> for done, cancelled and superseded. Superseded counts like cancelled in cut completeness. Test 2a includes a superseded goal.

output.summary: Revision 3 of the git-flow branching design. It fixes the four round-2 findings and leaves the approach unchanged. The release_sync and line_members_open waits are now computed by the frontier, from the upstream input and the closed-goal ledger, so they end on their own instead of hanging as recorded blocks. Hotfix lines run sync in record-only mode, so approve_finish is bound to the hotfix tip. Hotfix names are single-use, and the Closed trailer carries all three close reasons, with superseded counted like cancelled.

findings.text: test_engine_branching.FrontierTests.test_a_ready_workspace_op_is_blocked_while_base_restacks asserts run_tests is `ready` right after `s.reopen(1001, 'test_design')`. run_tests takes test_design.commands as a non-context input, so a reopened (not current) test_design blocks run_tests in pass 2, on the base engine too ('test_design not current'). In graph12 every agent workspace node produces an input of run_tests, so this graph cannot have a ready run_tests together with a ready agent. Rebuild the case on a graph where it can (for example a fixture graph whose op reads only implement.code.tree while another agent is ready), or check the pass-3 rewrite of a ready op on a hand-built state.

test_engine_branching.FrontierTests.test_release_sync_is_a_frontier_wait_that_ends_on_its_own: Sim fabricates the dependency's integrate output as pr = {'v': …}, with no `head`. So base's `heads` input (deps.integrate.pr.head) resolves as missing for the merged dependency, and base is `blocked`, not `ready`, once the release_sync wait ends. The first assertion now passes, because the wait is checked before the missing inputs. Give G1001 a real-shaped pr (s.step(1001, 'integrate', outputs={'pr': {'number': 1, 'url': 'u', 'head': s.sha(), 'tree': s.sha(), 'base': 'release/1'}, 'ci': {}})), or assert only that base is no longer waiting.

test_engine_branching.HotfixTests.test_member_waits_on_hotfix_start_then_merges_into_the_hotfix_branch calls self.discovery(m) and later self.done(m). done() calls deliver(), which runs discovery again, and `start design` refuses with not_ready ('design is current'). After hotfix start, continue from base (self.op(m, 'base') and the rest of deliver) instead of done().

test_engine_branching.LedgerTests.test_closed_goals_are_counted_from_trailers_alone runs `commit-tree -p <goal tip>` in the seed clone. The seed never fetched zzzops/goal/g<a>, so git fails before the engine runs. Fetch the goal ref into the seed first: s.git('fetch', '-q', 'origin', f'refs/heads/zzzops/goal/g{a}').

test_engine_branching.LedgerTests.test_legacy_closed_goals_are_read_in_one_batch compares git-process counts of two `next` runs. Only the first runs right after push_dev, so it also downloads the new policy commit, which shows in GIT_TRACE as pack-objects plus unpack-objects (24 vs 20 processes). That download is the only difference; the legacy documents are read through the one persistent cat-file --batch. Warm up with one `next` (or a fetch) before the first count, or count only cat-file and show processes.

output.summary: This change adds git-flow release lines behind an optional settings.branching block, which requires capability release_lines (engine 1.2.0, gated by engine.min). Without the block the engine behaves exactly as before, and the golden fingerprints are unchanged. It ships a second graph, `release` (approve_start, git.line_sync, approve_finish, git.line_finish), new verbs `release cut N` and `hotfix start X`, goal schema 2 with `flow`, trailer-based ledgers, goal targets in base, integrate, merge, cards, next and show, the effective release gate, frontier-computed waits (hotfix_start, release_sync, line_members_open) and a bounded scheduled restack (pass 3). SPEC and DESIGN are amended, a HISTORY §4 row is added and the G1025 pending row is deleted. The full suite passes except 5 frozen tests whose fixtures cannot pass on any engine; each is filed as a finding on test_design. Two side changes: the shipped POLICY placeholder integration_branch is now dev (a frozen test validates the template with production main), and test_engine_schemas counts the new `conflict` exit code.

findings.text: New 1 (major): the release_sync (§8) and line_members_open (§6) waits are recorded waiting_for: dependency blocks. frontier.py:243 keeps such a node waiting until its input_fp changes, and nothing changes it here. base's inputs exclude the target tip (G1021), so the sync landing never wakes the dependent, and pass 3 needs st[base] current. finish's inputs are unchanged when a late member is cancelled, a case the design itself names. Both hang forever. Fix: make both frontier-computed waits: base waits while some merges[d] is not an ancestor of the target tip, using the upstream input; finish waits from the ledger, like line_complete. Add tests: sync lands, then base runs; a late member is cancelled, then finish runs on the existing approval.

New 2: hotfix lines have no tip binding. With sync skipped (§7), approve_finish's only input sync.merged is the skipped placeholder, so the approval is not tied to hotfix/x's tip, and finish step 1's tip check is undefined. A member merged into hotfix/x after the approval goes to production unapproved, which is the attempt-1 problem (review_design:1:5) on hotfix lines. Fix: bind both line kinds to the line tip, e.g. sync in record-only mode on hotfix lines (merged = hotfix tip) or a small git.line_tip op that approve_finish and finish read. Test it.

New 3: a hotfix name cannot be reused after its line finishes. The hotfix-start key {line: hotfix, name: x} matches the closed line goal, so the verb returns it as recovered and never creates an open line. The kept hotfix/x (D14) remains, and a new member marked flow.hotfix = x waits forever on a repeating hotfix_start item. Fix: new/edit refuse a flow.hotfix that names a finished hotfix line (from the ledger's Line trailer) with a 'choose a new name' hint, or add a generation to the key and branch. Test it.

New 4 (minor): §3.1 writes 'Closed: done|cancelled', but closed.reason also allows superseded. Cut completeness must classify superseded goals from the trailer alone, or each one falls back to a document read or is miscounted. Fix: write Closed: <reason> for all three reasons, have D6 count superseded like cancelled, and add a superseded goal to test 2a.

output.summary: Approved. Revision 3 resolves review_design:2:1 to 2:4. The release_sync and line_members_open waits are now frontier-computed and end on their own, and a race at run time returns a time wait. Hotfix sync runs in record-only mode, so approve_finish is bound to the hotfix tip. Hotfix names are single-use. Closed: <reason> covers superseded. Round-1 findings stay resolved, and no new holes were found. Note: the capability is still named 'branching'; G1027 names it 'release_lines', which the implementer should use.

findings.response: fixed: test_trailers_are_written_with_branching closes a release-1 goal as superseded and asserts `Closed: superseded`; new CutItemTests.test_superseded_goal_neither_blocks_the_cut_nor_completes_the_release_alone. Also added the GOLDEN_FP regeneration rule (regenerate with the new base commit's engine, never the head).
findings.text: F2 (minor): superseded goals are not tested where design revision 3 promised. Rev 3 §13 test 2a says the cut counts done, cancelled and superseded goals from trailers alone, but LedgerTests asserts only 'Closed: cancelled' and 'Closed: done', and no cut test has a superseded release-N goal (only the frontier's line_members_open case uses superseded). Fix: close one release-1 goal as superseded in test_trailers_are_written_with_branching (assert 'Closed: superseded'), and in a cut-item test assert that it neither blocks the cut nor alone makes the release complete.

output.summary: Approved. review_tests:1:2 is resolved. The superseded-goal cut test now asserts 'no cut' while the superseded goal is the only release-1 goal, and creates `a` only afterwards. An implementation that counts superseded as done would now fail it. The 'does not block the cut' half and the 'Closed: superseded' trailer assertion are unchanged. 1:1 was already resolved. No new findings.

responses.implement:1:1: fixed: graph12 cannot have a ready agent beside a ready run_tests (every agent workspace node feeds run_tests). The test now adds a fixture workspace agent `notes` (reads design.doc and base.base_commit; run_tests does not read it) to the frozen graph, asserts notes and run_tests are both ready and base current before the target moves, then asserts both are blocked on `restack` with base ready(upstream). It still checks that pass 3 blocks a ready workspace op as well as an agent (§5.3, §13 item 5).
responses.implement:1:2: fixed: G1001's integrate is now stepped with a real-shaped pr {number, url, head, tree, base: release/1} and ci {}, so base's heads input resolves once the release_sync wait ends; the test still asserts waiting(release_sync) and then `ready` with no other change (§5.5, §13).
responses.implement:1:3: fixed: after `hotfix start`, the test continues from base (op base, test_design, review_tests, implement, run_tests, review_impl, integrate, approve_merge, merge) instead of done(), which re-ran discovery; it still asserts the merge closes the goal as done and the PR base is hotfix/<name>.
responses.implement:1:4: fixed: the seed fetches refs/heads/zzzops/goal/g<a> before commit-tree, as suggested.
responses.implement:1:5: fixed: one warm-up `next` runs before the first count, so both counted runs exclude the policy download; the equality of the two counts (no git call per closed legacy goal) and the batch bound are unchanged.

spec:
The owner's direction (2026-11-01), verbatim: "Ok I do want release management in R1. Here's how I see it working, we base it on git flow. When all R* goals are complete, we ask the user for approval to create a release branch according to git flow. When a release branch exists for a goal, the CLI should branch off of that tip, not dev. Constant rebasing can be avoided by the use of scheduled downstream merges. I'd propose that before starting work on a tip, the upstream tips are checked for changes, and if they exist a downstream merge is scheduled. All of this should be deploy/CI/actual release flow agnostic, it's just a branching strategy."

Today the engine has one integration branch (settings.integration_branch, here dev), every goal bases on it, a goal's release only gates its `merge` node (release_gate while release > settings.releases.current), and every move of dev makes `base` rebase the work branch. Nothing cuts or tracks a release.

Build a git-flow branching strategy into the engine:
1. Release cut. When every goal of release N is complete (closed done, or only waiting at a release gate), `next` shows a human item asking to create the release branch for N (git-flow naming, e.g. release/<N>, configurable) from the integration branch tip. Approving creates the branch and records it. Release N+1 goals then pass the release gate on the integration branch (decide in the design whether this is `releases.current` advancing or the release branch existing).
2. Base per goal. A goal whose release has a release branch bases on, integrates into and merges into that branch's tip, not the integration branch. Goals of later releases keep using the integration branch. Show each goal's target on cards, in `next` and in `show`.
3. Release finish. Finishing a release (git flow: merge the release branch into the production branch and back into the integration branch, then retire the release branch) is a human-approved item. Tags, versions, CI and deployment stay outside the engine.
4. Scheduled downstream merges instead of constant rebasing. Before work starts on a tip (a node of a goal, or a release branch), the engine checks the upstream tips for changes: the release branch's changes flow down to the integration branch, and a goal's target changes flow into its work branch. If upstream has new commits, a downstream merge is scheduled (a graph node or op that merges upstream into the downstream branch, with conflicts going to an agent as base conflicts do now), instead of rebasing on every move. Decide in the design how this replaces or coexists with `base`'s rebase, how checkpoints, `change` and staleness behave on merge commits (today's identity rules assume a rebased linear history), and how stacked goals (G1020-style) fit.
5. Branching only. No deploy, CI or release-publication behaviour: the engine creates, targets and merges branches, and leaves version tags, semantic-release, changelogs and deploys to the project.
6. Policy. Production branch name, release branch pattern and whether release branches are used at all are POLICY settings; a project without them keeps today's single-integration-branch behaviour.

Acceptance:
- Engine tests: the release-cut item appears only when release N is complete; approving creates the branch; a release-N goal created afterwards bases on and opens its PR against the release branch while a release-N+1 goal targets the integration branch; an upstream change schedules a downstream merge instead of a rebase, and a conflicting one becomes an agent item; finishing merges into production and back into the integration branch.
- A repository without the new settings behaves exactly as today (existing tests unchanged).
- This PR edits docs/design/SPEC.md and DESIGN.md for every contract change it makes and adds a HISTORY §4 row (G1017's rule).
- Release 1 of this repository is cut through this mechanism.
title: Release branching: git-flow release branches, goals based on their release's tip, scheduled downstream merges
